# dseupd

> Returns the converged Ritz values and (optionally) Ritz vectors for a symmetric eigenproblem from an ARPACK Lanczos factorization.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dseupd from '@rreusser/blahpack/arpack/dseupd';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dseupd(
    order,
    rvec,
    howmny,
    select, strideSelect,
    d, strideD,
    z, LDZ,
    sigma,
    bmat,
    N,
    which,
    nev,
    tol,
    resid, strideResid,
    ncv,
    v, LDV,
    iparam, strideIparam,
    ipntr, strideIpntr,
    workd,
    workl,
    lworkl
) → info: integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `rvec` | `boolean` | If `true`, compute Ritz vectors; if `false`, compute Ritz values only |
| `howmny` | `"all" \| "partial" \| "select"` | `'all'`, `'partial'`, or `'select'` (only `'all'` is implemented) |
| `select` | `Uint8Array`<br><sub>length ncv</sub> | **in/out** · Logical work array of length `ncv` |
| ↳ `strideSelect` | `integer` | Stride length for `select` |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nev</sub> | **out** · Output array for the Ritz values (length `nev`) |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| `z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>? × nev</sub> | **out** · Output matrix of Ritz vectors (N-by-nev when howmny is `'all'`) |
| ↳ `LDZ` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `z` |
| `sigma` | `number` | Shift used when the mode is 3, 4, or 5 |
| `bmat` | `"standard" \| "generalized"` | `'standard'` for a standard problem, `'generalized'` for a generalized problem |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Dimension of the eigenproblem |
| `which` | `"LM" \| "SM" \| "LA" \| "SA" \| "BE"` | Eigenvalue selection: `'LM'`, `'SM'`, `'LA'`, `'SA'`, or `'BE'` |
| `nev` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of eigenvalues requested |
| `tol` | `number` | Relative accuracy tolerance used by `dsaupd` |
| `resid` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Final residual vector (length N) |
| ↳ `strideResid` | `integer` | Stride length for `resid` |
| `ncv` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of Lanczos basis vectors |
| `v` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>? × ncv</sub> | **in/out** · Lanczos basis matrix (N-by-ncv); overwritten on exit |
| ↳ `LDV` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `v` |
| `iparam` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length 7</sub> | ARPACK parameter array (`iparam[4]`=nconv, `iparam[6]`=mode) |
| ↳ `strideIparam` | `integer` | Stride length for `iparam` |
| `ipntr` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length 11</sub> | **in/out** · ARPACK pointer array into `workl` |
| ↳ `strideIpntr` | `integer` | Stride length for `ipntr` |
| `workd` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ 2 * N</sub> | Work array of length `2*N` |
| `workl` | `Float64Array \| null` | **in/out** · Private work array set by `dsaupd` (length `lworkl`); modified on exit |
| `lworkl` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Length of `workl` |

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 on success; a negative error code otherwise

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "all", "partial", "select"
- `TypeError` eleventh argument must be one of the following: "standard", "generalized"
- `TypeError` thirteenth argument must be one of the following: "LM", "SM", "LA", "SA", "BE"
- `TypeError` `howmny` must be one of `all`, `partial`, or `select`
- `TypeError` `bmat` must be one of `standard` or `generalized`
- `TypeError` `which` must be one of `LM`, `SM`, `LA`, `SA`, or `BE`
- `RangeError` `workd` array must have sufficient length
- `RangeError` `workl` array must have sufficient length

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dseupd.ndarray(
    rvec,
    howmny,
    select, strideSelect, offsetSelect,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    z, strideZ1, strideZ2, offsetZ,
    sigma,
    bmat,
    N,
    which,
    nev,
    tol,
    resid, strideResid, offsetResid,
    ncv,
    v, strideV1, strideV2, offsetV,
    iparam, strideIparam, offsetIparam,
    ipntr, strideIpntr, offsetIpntr,
    workd, strideWorkd, offsetWorkd,
    workl, strideWorkl, offsetWorkl,
    lworkl
) → info: integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `rvec` | `boolean` | If `true`, compute Ritz vectors; if `false`, compute Ritz values only |
| `howmny` | `"all" \| "partial" \| "select"` | `'all'`, `'partial'`, or `'select'` (only `'all'` is implemented) |
| `select` | `Uint8Array`<br><sub>length ncv</sub> | **in/out** · Logical work array of length `ncv` |
| ↳ `strideSelect` | `integer` | Stride length for `select` |
| ↳ `offsetSelect` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `select` |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length nev</sub> | **out** · Output array for the Ritz values (length `nev`) |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `d` |
| `z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>? × nev</sub> | **out** · Output matrix of Ritz vectors (N-by-nev when howmny is `'all'`) |
| ↳ `strideZ1` | `integer` | Stride of the first (row) dimension of `z` |
| ↳ `strideZ2` | `integer` | Stride of the second (column) dimension of `z` |
| ↳ `offsetZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `z` |
| `sigma` | `number` | Shift used when the mode is 3, 4, or 5 |
| `bmat` | `"standard" \| "generalized"` | `'standard'` for a standard problem, `'generalized'` for a generalized problem |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Dimension of the eigenproblem |
| `which` | `"LM" \| "SM" \| "LA" \| "SA" \| "BE"` | Eigenvalue selection: `'LM'`, `'SM'`, `'LA'`, `'SA'`, or `'BE'` |
| `nev` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of eigenvalues requested |
| `tol` | `number` | Relative accuracy tolerance used by `dsaupd` |
| `resid` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Final residual vector (length N) |
| ↳ `strideResid` | `integer` | Stride length for `resid` |
| ↳ `offsetResid` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `resid` |
| `ncv` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of Lanczos basis vectors |
| `v` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>? × ncv</sub> | **in/out** · Lanczos basis matrix (N-by-ncv); overwritten on exit |
| ↳ `strideV1` | `integer` | Stride of the first (row) dimension of `v` |
| ↳ `strideV2` | `integer` | Stride of the second (column) dimension of `v` |
| ↳ `offsetV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `v` |
| `iparam` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length 7</sub> | ARPACK parameter array (`iparam[4]`=nconv, `iparam[6]`=mode) |
| ↳ `strideIparam` | `integer` | Stride length for `iparam` |
| ↳ `offsetIparam` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `iparam` |
| `ipntr` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length 11</sub> | **in/out** · ARPACK pointer array into `workl` |
| ↳ `strideIpntr` | `integer` | Stride length for `ipntr` |
| ↳ `offsetIpntr` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `ipntr` |
| `workd` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ 2 * N</sub> | Work array of length `2*N` |
| ↳ `strideWorkd` | `integer` | Stride length for `workd` |
| ↳ `offsetWorkd` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `workd` |
| `workl` | `Float64Array` | **in/out** · Private work array set by `dsaupd` (length `lworkl`); modified on exit |
| ↳ `strideWorkl` | `integer` | Stride length for `workl` |
| ↳ `offsetWorkl` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `workl` |
| `lworkl` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Length of `workl` |

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 on success; a negative error code otherwise

**Throws**

- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "all", "partial", "select"
- `TypeError` fourteenth argument must be one of the following: "standard", "generalized"
- `TypeError` sixteenth argument must be one of the following: "LM", "SM", "LA", "SA", "BE"
- `TypeError` `howmny` must be one of `all`, `partial`, or `select`
- `TypeError` `bmat` must be one of `standard` or `generalized`
- `TypeError` `which` must be one of `LM`, `SM`, `LA`, `SA`, or `BE`
- `RangeError` `workd` array must have sufficient length
- `RangeError` `workl` array must have sufficient length

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import Uint8Array from '@stdlib/array/uint8/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlamch from '../../../lapack/dlamch/lib/index.js';
import dsaupd from '../dsaupd/lib/index.js';
import dseupd from '@rreusser/blahpack/arpack/dseupd';

// `dseupd` post-processes a converged ARPACK Lanczos factorization produced by
// `dsaupd`. First run the `dsaupd` reverse-communication loop on the 10x10
// 1-D Laplacian (OP = A, B = I) to find its 3 largest eigenvalues:
const n = 10;
const nev = 3;
const ncv = 6;
const A = new Float64Array( n * n );
let i;
for ( i = 0; i < n; i++ ) {
	A[ i + ( i * n ) ] = 2.0;
	if ( i < n - 1 ) {
		A[ i + ( ( i + 1 ) * n ) ] = -1.0;
		A[ ( i + 1 ) + ( i * n ) ] = -1.0;
	}
}

const v = new Float64Array( n * ncv );
const resid = new Float64Array( n );
for ( i = 0; i < n; i++ ) {
	resid[ i ] = 1.0 + ( 0.1 * ( i + 1 ) );
}
const workd = new Float64Array( 3 * n );
const lworkl = ( ncv * ncv ) + ( 8 * ncv );
const workl = new Float64Array( lworkl );
const iparam = new Int32Array( 11 );
iparam[ 0 ] = 1; // exact shifts
iparam[ 2 ] = 100; // max iterations
iparam[ 6 ] = 1; // mode 1
const ipntr = new Int32Array( 11 );
const ido = new Int32Array( 1 );
const state = {};
const tol = dlamch( 'epsilon' ); // relative accuracy (machine precision)

// Reverse-communication loop; info=1 signals a user-supplied initial residual.
let info = 1;
let p, q, r, c, acc;
do {
	info = dsaupd( 'column-major', state, ido, 'standard', n, 'LM', nev, tol, resid, 1, ncv, v, n, iparam, 1, ipntr, 1, workd, workl, lworkl, info );
	if ( ido[ 0 ] === -1 || ido[ 0 ] === 1 ) {
		p = ipntr[ 0 ];
		q = ipntr[ 1 ];
		for ( r = 0; r < n; r++ ) {
			acc = 0.0;
			for ( c = 0; c < n; c++ ) {
				acc += A[ r + ( c * n ) ] * workd[ p + c ];
			}
			workd[ q + r ] = acc;
		}
	}
} while ( ido[ 0 ] !== 99 );

const select = new Uint8Array( ncv );
const d = new Float64Array( nev );
const z = new Float64Array( n * nev );

const howmny = 'all'; // compute all Ritz vectors
const bmat = 'standard'; // standard eigenproblem

// Extract the three largest eigenvalues and their Ritz vectors:
info = dseupd( 'column-major', true, howmny, select, 1, d, 1, z, n, 0.0, bmat, n, 'LM', nev, tol, resid, 1, ncv, v, n, iparam, 1, ipntr, 1, workd, workl, lworkl );

console.log( info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => 0

console.log( Array.prototype.slice.call( d ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => three largest eigenvalues of the 1-D Laplacian, ascending

console.log( 'exact:', [ 8, 9, 10 ].map( function lam( k ) { // eslint-disable-line no-console
	return 2.0 - ( 2.0 * Math.cos( k * Math.PI / ( n + 1 ) ) );
}) );
```
